Recipe:
No-Sugar-Added Wild Blackberry Jam 3 pints Basic
§ion;
In Washington, we have wild blackberries growing everywhere. One year, we decided to make jam, and since Ransom is diabetic, we tried making some without sugar for him to enjoy. It has a more solid texture than the regular jam, but it tastes great!
Wild BlackberriesMashed 5 CupsRequires ≈7-8 Cups fresh berries
SucraloseSuch as Splenda 2½ Cups
Lemon Juice¼ Cup No-Sugar-Needed Pectin1 1.75-oz. Package
Remove any stems from berries Let berries soak in a large bowl, and pick out grass, leaves, etc. that floats to the top. Drain, then rinse berries in a strainer or colander. Mash berries, using a potato masher or something similar.
Put Mashed Wild Blackberries into a large pot, add Lemon Juice and mix well. Bring berry mixture to a boil. In a separate bowl, mix Sucralose and No-Sugar-Needed Pectin. When berry mixture is boiling, slowly mix in Sucralose/Pectin mixture and stir until well dissolved. Bring mixture to a boil again, and boil for 1 minute, then remove from heat immediately. Follow instructions in the Bath Canning: How-To section.
Cooking time in Bath Canner:
Altitude Time
Below 1000 feet 5 minutes
1000-6000 feet 10 minutes
Above 6000 feet 15 minutes
If you let the jam boil too long, it will not "set" and you end up with runny syrup instead of jam.
We do not recommend using liquid pectin. When we do, we have had problems getting it to set.
Instead of mashing fruit, you can place fruit in a blender and blend it for a few seconds until it is just barely liquefied. The Lemon Juice raises the acidity level of the jam so it will not spoil when stored. If you have a big enough pot, there is no reason that you can't double the recipe.
If you are not going to can the jam, the Lemon Juice can be left out.
